newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Baltic presidents urge NATO promise on new members.
newsitem.headline: Baltic presidents urge NATO promise on new members.

text.p: The presidents of the three Baltic states, likely to be shut out of an early round of NATO expansion, on Monday asked the alliance for a commitment that other new members be accepted later.
They issued a declaration reaffirming their desire to join NATO as the alliance's leaders prepared to head for Paris for the signing on May 27 of a historic accord setting out relations with Russia.
On the same day, the Baltic presidents are also due to hold a regional summit with Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski and Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma.
Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas, Latvia's Guntis Ulmanis and Estonian President Lennart Meri appealed to NATO members to show "continuity" in NATO enlargement.

In their declaration, they asked the alliance: "To make a commitment to invite subsequent members to join NATO either before or when new states are admitted and to provide for a regular review of the enlargement process."

The Balts, independent for six years from the former Soviet Union, are anxious for NATO entry as they seek to break a cycle of history where they have come under the domination of more powerful neighbours, particularly Russia.

The leaders, meeting in the southern Estonian town of Otepaa, some 220 km (136 miles) from the capital Tallinn, also asked for support for their countries to join NATO and an institutional accession process.
The Balts are among those likely to be disappointed when NATO invites new members at a July summit in Madrid with favourites regarded as the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland.

Moscow continues to object strongly to the inclusion of the Balts or any other former Soviet republic. The U.S. has also said that the Baltic armies are too weak to defend other NATO states, a key part of the alliance's treaty.
